about: The Mining Ship layer table (rd wave 1 Task 7; spec section 12): one row per file in firmware/apps/rd/assets/. tools/rd_export.mjs draws the rows in headless Chrome from the designers' mockups (read in place from $RD_DESIGN; the closure-private builders reached through tools/export/rd_export.js's exposure shim, never an edit of the design files) and from our own drawing of a cited recipe; tools/rd_pack.py packs them. Row keys: name (rd_ + at most 12 characters; committed bytes keep their own), face (a key of rd/faces.h's ids, or shared), kind (rgb565, rgb565a8, a8 or a8_strip: a bin or an A8 strip of a mockup's canvas tagged fn while mockup is driven, or of call, an exposed builder called on a w x h canvas, tiled when tile is set; atlas: one A8 plane; atlas2: glow and core planes of one cell table, ATL2; thumb: the mockup face's settled frame at pinned.thumb_t_ms, 68 px in the circle), source (the citation). An atlas row draws its glyphs with draw: stencil (the reveal mockup's painted stencil(), its own recipe and seed per glyph), stroke (an outline of line px, join), fill, or phosphor (glow: blur px at alpha a, then the core); advance time gives the digits the mockups' fixed advance (timeMetrics), the colon its own and the dash 0.66 x the digit advance, natural each glyph its own width; extra adds glyphs drawn another way under their own codes (as). Rows with crc32 are committed bytes (packed elsewhere, checked by pixel CRC-32). Stasis Clock's face has no rows of its own: its base (the seal arcs, ticks, rivets and lamp housing) is drawn procedurally at bind (RW10), and the rest of it is the shared atlases. Its reveal, Stasis Release (Task 10), has four: rd_st_lid, rd_st_lidf, rd_st_haz and rd_st_frost, each cut from the mockup's own lid builder (build: an exposed builder that returns its canvas, drawn at 466 px; crop; and a8: a ramp index, a tint's coverage over a base, or the delta between two of the builder's results). Ship Terminal (Task 11) has one, rd_tm_house: the canvas its build() makes while the face is driven (fn, as dw's bin rows), cut to row.crop and indexed on its ramp (a8, as rd_st_lid). Hull Plate (Task 13) has three: rd_hp_plate (the lit plate, the second canvas plateTexture() makes: pick), rd_hp_marks (build()'s canvas over that plate, a8.over: each byte a colour and an alpha of its runs) and rd_hp_patch (an rgb565 crop of build()'s canvas). Bunk Clock (Task 14) has two: rd_bk_case (an rgb565 crop of the buildBg() canvas the face makes while driven) and rd_bk_shelf (one column of the same canvas, the shelf's rows); its card blanks are drawn at bind from cardFace()'s recipe, and its lamp is procedural. Curry Clock (Task 15) has two: rd_cu_tray (an rgb565 crop of the buildBg() canvas, cut to the tray's disc: disc), rd_cu_lid (the buildLid() card, a ramp index, cut to its disc) (wave 1 also had the steam's glowSprite() blob, its alpha: wave 1's procedural steam drew it, and the host tests' oracle of that steam, rd_cu_steam_oracle.c, still holds its bytes); wave 2 Task 12 replaced the blob with rd_cu_wisp (kind a8_rows: the steam as a pre-rendered per-wisp loop, row.wisp, our own drawing of steam()'s recipe from that blob, packed as ARW1: each row's extent and its bytes); its heat sticker is drawn at bind from sticker()'s recipe, and its hands, chillies and ticks are polygons. Bay Mouth (wave 2 Task 3) has two: rd_by_star (an rgb565 crop of bayBase()'s canvas as it stood before the door frame's lip, build.before; max writes its largest channel into assets_meta.h as ASSET_RD_BY_STAR_MAX) and rd_by_ring (hazardRing()'s canvas as an A8 polar strip of 1 420 columns, row.polar); its upper stars, the lip, its rivets and the hazard ring's dark pass are procedural. Its airlock (wave 2 Task 4) has two: rd_by_doors (buildAirDoors()'s canvas, a ramp index, as rd_st_lid) and rd_by_kick (an rgb565 crop of the same canvas, the kick plate's rows); the lamp, the starlight, the beacon and the dust are the reveal's own drawing. Drift Plate (wave 2 Task 5) has two: rd_dp_tile (buildHullTile()'s canvas, an rgb565 row drawn at its own 466 x 186 by build.dest; max as rd_by_star) and rd_dp_wash (washMe()'s canvas, a8: the strokes' coverage of their colour over black); its stars, its windows, its frame numbers and the pass itself are the face's own drawing. Drive Console (wave 2 Task 6) has two: rd_dc_panel (the canvas its build() makes while driven, a ramp index of five runs, as rd_dk_frame) and rd_dc_cuts (an rgb565 crop of the same canvas, the tapes); its lamps, digits, colon, strip, needles, collar and button are the face's own drawing. Nav Scope (wave 2 Task 7) has two: rd_sc_giant (an rgb565 crop of the giantSprite() canvas the face makes while driven, its top-left 284 x 150) and rd_sc_dial (the canvas its build() makes while driven with numerals()'s paintSprite() sprites replayed over it, row.sprites, as a8.runs over black: each byte a colour and an alpha); its corona's breath, the wake's warm-up, the sweep and its afterglow fan, the contacts, the readout, the cursors and the hub are the face's own drawing. Vending Machine (wave 2 Task 8) has one: rd_vm_front (an rgb565 crop of the buildBg() canvas the face makes while driven: the bezel, the buttons and their names, the coin slot and the tray over the mockup's own fascia); the fascia beyond it is the shared rd_grime tinted hull-dark, and its lightbox, digits and their glow, ticker, lamps, sticker, flap and the vended item are the face's own drawing. the Bowl (wave 2 Task 9) has one: rd_cb_bowl (an rgb565 crop of the buildBg() canvas the face makes while driven, cut to the bowl's disc: the lip with its chips and painted numerals, the wall and the polished floor engraved MINE); its kibbles, crumbs, fish hands, hub, paw, stale marker and unset lines are the face's own drawing. Mop Bot (wave 2 Task 10) has one: rd_mb_tread (an rgb565 crop of the buildBg() canvas the face makes while driven, its top-left 44 x 44 corner, past the grime's and the ticks' reach: one period of the tread plate, whose plates alternate their tilt with the parity of column plus row, so the plate repeats every 44 px each way); the face tiles it under every clip, tints the shared rd_grime over it, and draws the ticks, the clean wet arc, the boot prints, the hazard ring, the sign, the robot and the lines itself.

rows.name: rd_mb_tread
rows.source: spec 10.13 Mop Bot's deck (the ruling C5: a repeating tread tile plus the shared grime A8 tinted, about 2 KB; notes-quarters.md section 5 Device: the 22 x 44 tread tile path); faces-quarters.js:836-839 buildBg() (the #0b0c0d deck and its tread plate: an 8 x 2.2 #1b1e21 ellipse every 22 px, odd rows offset 11, each tilted +-.6 rad by the parity of its column plus its row, with its rgba(138, 144, 150, .08) highlight), the canvas the face makes while driven, cut to its top-left 44 x 44 corner (the nearest pixel 267 px from the centre: past the 280 grime ellipses' reach, r 232 plus 32, and the ticks', r 229), on black. The tilt's parity makes the period 44 x 44, not the notes' 22 x 44: a 22 px step flips every plate's tilt (rd_core/mopbot.c tiles it by x mod 44 and y mod 44)
